page.layout: One printed page (left, p. 260) with running head at top, main text in one column, and a narrow column of marginal notes at the right edge (cut off, largely unreadable, from the facing page). No text below the main text.

main_text.p: Nox ipsa, quæ fores obsidet cui alto Silentio, quo Majestatem Æ&tui conciliet, circumfundit ali quid de superstitioso Terrore. Quin igitur in seram vesperam differas Convivium, si tantus luxus, tantillo parari possit impendio. Tunc etiam animus noster qui interdiu in diversa dispergitur, curis jam defunctus, conferet se totum intra triclinium: retrahensque se ab atra illa, quæ terras undique cælumque tenet solitudine, gestiet ad candelarum facu-las, insolitâ quadam, quæ meridiem non novit, ac titillante lætitiâ: Intempestâ ceu fortè nocte Insomnes pueri, mille timent lemurum ludibria, donec correptâ stragulâ obvolvant caput, tremulo jam gaudio sollicitante corculum, quod confusum illud Silentum chaos, qui minitabant stra-
main_text.notes: Marginal notes at the right edge are cut off and only partly legible (fragments such as "exe", "exemplo", "sed"); they are not transcribed. Several words at the line ends of the main text are hyphenated across lines as printed. The first line of the page reads "Nox ipsa" as the continuation of the text from the previous page, so the first paragraph is marked as continuing.
